- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 75→79, 79→83) — model peaks too high and then corrects too slowly.
- Underestimates in late forecast period (last 5–10 days of 30d) — model fails to capture sustained upward momentum or late-stage volatility.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to prior mean too quickly, underestimating persistence of trends.
- Lagged response: model reacts too slowly to recent price changes — especially when history shows accelerating trends.
- Overconfidence in short-term momentum: model overweights recent spikes and underweights long-term mean or seasonal patterns.
- Avoid extrapolating from single recent peak — model often assumes trend continues from last 3–5 days, ignoring potential reversal or consolidation.
